title: HTTP contract, event contract and observed behavior
question: How does an accepted request become a completed business operation?

steps.title: The interface is a declaration
steps.narration: Operation name, request, response and authorization requirements belong to the versioned interface. A contract does not prove a deployment or successful call.

steps.title: Accepted is not completed
steps.narration: HTTP acceptance and event publication are distinct milestones. This illustrative scenario assumes an outbox or equivalent consistency policy would be specified; it is not implemented here.

steps.title: Delivery and processing are separate
steps.narration: A redelivery may repeat the same event. Deduplication, transaction boundaries, ordering and compensation require their own explicit contracts.
questions: What uniquely identifies one event and one processing attempt?
What happens if writing succeeds but acknowledgement fails?

steps.title: A trace has stronger structure than an animation
steps.narration: Actual telemetry needs trace/span identities, links and timestamps from a producer. Clock order alone is not causality; an authored animation cannot supply a missing span.
